newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on political rumours.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on political rumours.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit taking, Thai stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday after investors bought shares on rumours that former premier Chatichai Choonhavan might become the new prime minister, brokers said.

The SET index, which hit its intraday low at 1,021.20 at the lunch break, rose after the market resumed in the afternoon session and ended 7.84 points higher at 1,042.21. Turnover was worth about five billion baht.
"Investors gained more confidence after the rumours spread in the market that Chatichai would become the new prime minister," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.

Chatichai, now leader of opposition Chart Pattana Party, was seen as a compromise candidate to replace outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa, brokers said. Banharn said on Saturday he would step down in seven days after choosing an appropiate successor. The resignation was in exchange for support from coalition partners in a no-confidence vote.
"The index rose after investors bought stocks, especially in the banking sector, on their belief that Chatichai and the new ministers could could solve some economic problems," said Virat.

Bank and finance issues were actively traded on the bourse with large capitalised Bangkok Bank topping the list, gaining four baht to 218. Finance One rose three to 102 and Nava Finance and Securities advanced 2.50 to 57.50.
Among the top losers were STA Group (1993) which fell 2.75 baht to 26.25 and and Minor Corp which dipped 2.25 to 20.75.
Support is seen at 1,037-point while resistance was at 1,055 on Wednesday, brokers said.
